title: Wildcard Pattern Matching
description: Given an input string `s` and a pattern `p`, implement wildcard pattern matching with support for '?' and '*' where '?' matches any single character and '*' matches any sequence of characters (including empty sequence).
input_format: Two lines: first string `s`, second pattern `p`.
hints: Wildcard '*' can match 0 to any number of characters.
Use a greedy approach with backtracking on the last seen star position.
When mismatch occurs, retry the last '*' matching one more character.

reference_solution:
import sys
lines = sys.stdin.read().split()
s = lines[0] if len(lines) > 0 else ''
p = lines[1] if len(lines) > 1 else ''
i = j = 0
star_idx = -1
match = 0
while i < len(s):
    if j < len(p) and (p[j] == '?' or p[j] == s[i]):
        i += 1; j += 1
    elif j < len(p) and p[j] == '*':
        star_idx = j
        match = i
        j += 1
    elif star_idx != -1:
        j = star_idx + 1
        match += 1
        i = match
    else:
        print('false')
        sys.exit(0)
while j < len(p) and p[j] == '*': j += 1
print('true' if j == len(p) else 'false')
